messages:
alex: Customer (Acme Corp) reporting invalid JSON when using streaming structured output (stream=true, structured_output=\"json\"). Parser error: \"Unexpected end of JSON input\". Repro attached below.

mia: Thanks — can you paste the request_id + SDK / curl you used and a raw example of the stream chunks?

alex: request_id=req_0a1b2c, node-sdk v3.2. Repro curl: 
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-4","stream":true,"structured_output":"json","input":"generate profile"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

alex: Raw stream received (exact data events we got):
```
data: {"id":"tok1","delta":{"text":"{"}}

data: {"id":"tok1","delta":{"text":"\"name\":\"Alice\",\"city\":\"SF\","}}

data: {"id":"tok1","delta":{"text":"\"age\":30"}}

// client then tries to JSON.parse on concatenated text and fails with Unexpected end of JSON input
```

carlos: That looks like the final closing brace is never streamed. Any server logs showing close reason? Could be early connection close (client disconnect) or our stream ended without sending a final chunk.

eng-ml: Quick check — is this via HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1? HTTP/2 flush semantics differ and clients occasionally interpret stream end differently. Also, are you assembling the chunks verbatim (i.e., concatenating delta.text) or expecting each data event to be a complete JSON object?

alex: It's HTTP/2 from their Node app. We concatenated delta.text into a buffer and then JSON.parse(buffer) after [DONE]. The parse throws.

carlos: Server log snippet for req_0a1b2c: 
```
[2025-03-08T16:04:21Z] req=req_0a1b2c stream_start bytes_sent=120 status=200
[2025-03-08T16:04:23Z] req=req_0a1b2c stream_close reason=client_disconnect bytes_sent=492 status=499
```

support-bot: Escalated to eng-oncall: INC-4321. Assigned to eng-ml.

eng-ml: Thanks. Initial hypothesis: client closed connection before we emitted the final closing token. Two things to confirm: 1) Does the client receive a trailing data event with [DONE] or equivalent? (looks like not). 2) Is the client using a streaming JSON reassembler that can tolerate partial objects (we should recommend defensive parsing).

mia: Can you ask the customer to try two quick things and report back: 1) retry the same request with --http1.1 in curl (or force HTTP/1.1 in Node) to rule out HTTP/2 flushing; 2) add a small timeout on the client before aborting so it waits for final chunk.

alex: Customer tried switching to non-streaming (stream=false) and it returns valid JSON — so payload itself is fine. They also tried HTTP/1.1 and saw the same error intermittently.

eng-ml: Another workaround: stream into a line-delimited JSON format on the client side (emit a separator between objects) OR wait for explicit [DONE] marker from the API and only then attempt to JSON.parse. We should also instrument server to always send a final newline-delimited closing chunk even on abrupt client disconnect, but that is an infra change.

ops-oncall: For immediate debugging we need: full tcpdump/pcap of the session (customer permission), or at minimum server side trace showing TLS session close reason and whether FIN was sent by client. Also check for any proxy or load balancer between client and us that might tear the stream.

mia: Filed a customer-facing note: please try the client-side parse-safety workaround (accumulate until [DONE] token, then parse) and provide a trace if the issue persists. Escalation ticket link: INC-4321.

alex: Will share logs and try the parse-safety patch. Customer is asking for ETA — any chance to prioritise a graceful final-chunk fix?

eng-ml: We don't have a patch timeline yet. I'll triage INC-4321 tomorrow AM; if we can reproduce internally with an HTTP/2 client that closes early, we'll push a hotfix to ensure the final JSON closing bytes are emitted server-side. For now advise customers to use non-streaming or resilient parsing.

alex: OK thanks — I'll update the customer and attach this thread and the workaround steps.
